title: How Servers Run Software
summary: Connect hardware, operating systems, processes, files, users, and services.
objectives: Explain the role of an operating system.
Trace how hardware and software cooperate to provide a service.

vocab.def: Software that manages hardware and provides a platform for applications.
The organized way an operating system stores and finds files.

sections.heading: The operating system is a manager
sections.body: An operating system manages hardware, files, users, processes, and networking. Applications use the operating system instead of controlling every hardware detail themselves.

sections.heading: From request to service
sections.body: A request reaches a network interface, the operating system passes work to a process, and the process uses memory, storage, and the CPU to produce a response. These layers cooperate.

sections.heading: Windows and Linux
sections.body: Windows and Linux are operating systems with different tools and conventions. Neither is automatically best for every context. A safe sandbox lets students explore without touching production systems.

practice.prompt: Put these ideas in order: application process, network request, operating system, hardware resources, response. Explain the relationship.

quiz.question: What is one job of an operating system?
options: Manage hardware and provide a platform for applications
quiz.answer: Manage hardware and provide a platform for applications
